scenes.headline: How DSpark makes DeepSeek-V4 decode faster
scenes.sub: It drafts better and verifies smarter, without changing an output token
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Heather! DSpark isn't a new DeepSeek model. It's a module that makes DeepSeek V4 generate faster, without changing a single output token.

scenes.text: DSpark improves both halves of speculative decoding: a drafter that guesses better, and a verifier that checks only what will likely survive.
scenes.mark: checks only what will likely survive
scenes.say: DSpark improves both halves of the loop: a drafter that guesses better, and a verifier that only checks what's likely to survive.

scenes.title: The cost of one token
scenes.say: Speculative decoding's cost per token looks like this.

parts.note: a cheap drafter proposes a block of tokens
parts.say: A cheap drafter proposes a block.

parts.note: the target checks the whole block in one pass
parts.say: The big model verifies it in one pass.

parts.note: accepted length: agreed prefix plus one free bonus token
parts.say: G is the accepted length. Raise it, or verify smarter, and every token gets cheaper. The output never changes.

steps.say: From the target's last token, a parallel backbone, DFlash, drafts the whole block in one forward pass.
A tiny Markov head lets each position see the token sampled just before it. So after 'of' comes 'course', not 'problem'.
A calibrated confidence head scores how likely each prefix is to survive. The scheduler reads live load, and trims the unlikely tail when the GPU is busy.
The target verifies what's left in one pass, keeps the matching prefix, and corrects the first miss for free.

scenes.title: Accepted length gain per round
scenes.say: The Markov head pays off: accepted length rises about twenty-seven to thirty-one percent over EAGLE-3, and sixteen to eighteen over DFlash.

scenes.label: faster per-user generation at matched throughput, on V4-Flash and V4-Pro
scenes.note: the +661% point is one strict operating regime
scenes.say: In production, at matched throughput, per-user speed rises fifty-seven to eighty-five percent. The six hundred sixty-one percent figure is one strict regime, not a typical speedup.

scenes.text: Verification capacity is the scarce resource under load. A calibrated confidence score lets you spend it only where tokens will survive.
scenes.mark: spend it only where tokens will survive
scenes.say: Under load, verification is the scarce resource. A calibrated confidence score lets you spend it only on tokens likely to survive.

recap: A parallel block plus a tiny Markov head
A calibrated scheduler trims what gets verified
scenes.say: To recap: draft in parallel, thread one step of order back in, and verify only what will likely survive.
